name: Cronkhill

dates.altered: The list entry records that the house incorporates a smaller C17 and C18 house, that the service wing to the south is C17 with a C18 wing at the rear and a circa 1802 refacing to the east, and that 'Earlier photographs of the house show painted imitation oeils-de-boeuf windows to the top storey of the tower, now painted over'. The English Wikipedia article says that in 2016 the National Trust undertook a major restoration of the house.
dates.note: Historic England's entry gives 1802 flatly. The National Trust's own page says 'designed by the renowned Regency architect John Nash between 1802 and 1805'. Both are recorded; neither is resolved.

refs.title: Cronkhill - Wikipedia
refs.note: Read as continuous prose in an extract on 2026-09-05: 'Cronkhill, Atcham, Shropshire, designed by John Nash, is "the earliest Italianate villa in England".' The article footnotes that sentence to Newman and Pevsner, The Buildings of England: Shropshire, pp. 240-1; the phrase is therefore theirs at one remove and no facsimile of it has been read here. The same article states the plan the list entry states differently: 'The body of the house is a rectangular two-storey block, with a circular, three-storey, tower to the north and a square, three-storey, tower to the west.'

survey.prepared: Historic England names no author and the entry says 'The contents of this record have been generated from a legacy data system.' British Listed Buildings' rendering of the same entry prints 'Listing Date: 29 January 1952' and 'Grade: I'; a Historic England search result read the same day printed 'Date first listed: 29-Jan-1952'. No date of most recent amendment was found on either surface.

quotes.text: Plinth, deep eaves with paired brackets; integral brick stacks to towers.

Glazing bar sashes, round-arched to first floor. Central block of 2 bays with one bay returning to left; first-floor arched window and 3 ground- floor 15-pane sashes to front; round-arched loggia of 6 x 4 bays on 2 steps with chamfered square piers, moulded dentil cornice, and balustraded parapet.
quotes.page: Official list entry 1176915, Details; 'ground- floor' is broken by a hyphen and a space in the extract and is transcribed as it stands.

quotes.text: Timber framed, extended in red brick to west and refaced and eaves raised to east; slate roofs. T-plan. 2 storeys and 2 storeys and gable-lit attic. Central brick ridge stack and external brick end stack to wing. Framing: square panels, 5 from sole- plate to wall-plate; short straight corner braces. East front: 5 bays; round-arched glazing bar sashes.

note: Tranche 3, Italian rural vernacular cluster, 5 September 2026. Added by this pass, and it is the one record in the cluster that is not in Italy. It is here because this node's own period block names the British Italianate villa as a revival phase with `revival_node: null` -- no other node in the corpus owns Cronkhill, and the node's own long description argues from it: 'When Nash built Cronkhill in Shropshire in 1802 with a round tower and a bracketed eave, he was not quoting Palladio; he was quoting a painting of a Roman Campagna farm.' It is also, by a wide margin, the best-described building in the cluster: a Historic England Details section states materials, plan, storeys, eaves, bracket arrangement, bay counts and pane counts, where the Italian records state none of these.
